body.statement: If \((\kappa_{m,n}+1)\varepsilon_{m,n}+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t_{m,n}+d_{m,n}=o_{\Pr}(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal C_n\), then \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal C_n}|\Pr_{\mathbb P}(\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\mid\mathcal F_n)-(1-\alpha)|\to0\) for each prespecified mode \(m\in\{\mathrm{dir},\mathrm{rec}\}\), with no lower eigenvalue condition on \(R_{m,n}\). The rates in Theorems \(\mathrm{thm{:}stacked\mbox{-}orthogonal\mbox{-}expansion}\) and \(\mathrm{thm{:}relative\mbox{-}gram\mbox{-}rate}\), together with Gaussian comparison, verify the premise at \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\). This strictly strengthens Shen's fixed-summary pointwise interval within the declared selected-training class by covering all \(H_n\) conditional means jointly.
body.justification: This is the headline feasible simultaneous-coverage result and explicitly accounts for remainder, studentization, and multiplier-law errors.
body.gap: Shen (2026, Corollary 2 and Section 6) gives pointwise inference for prespecified fixed-horizon summaries, while Belloni et al. (2018) does not derive the TWSF score and covariance inputs. Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) compares direct and recursive panel-VAR forecasts by asymptotic MSPE, but does not construct a causal selected-training score, a feasible cross-lead Gram covariance, or a simultaneous conditional-mean ribbon.
body.consumer: It turns the daily conditional-mean forecasts used in Shen's NFL-stadium analysis into one jointly interpretable path ribbon; cumulative paths require a separately transformed covariance audit.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a prespecified mode and condition on \((\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})\).  Define
\[
 T_n=\max_{\ell\le H_n}\left|G_{m,n,\ell}/s_{m,n,\ell}\right|,
 \qquad F_n(x)=\Pr(T_n\le x\mid\mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n}).
\]
The variance floor makes every marginal variance positive.  Thus \(F_n\) is continuous even if \(R_{m,n}\) is singular, because \(\{T_n=x\}\) lies in a finite union of zero-probability events \(\{|G_{m,n,\ell}|=xs_{m,n,\ell}\}\).

Let \(\widehat F_n\) be the multiplier distribution function and \(\widehat c_n\) its lower \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile.  On
\[
 \varepsilon_{m,n}\le e,\qquad t_{m,n}\le t<1/2,\qquad
 d_{m,n}\le d<\tfrac12\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\},                         \tag{25}
\]
put
\[
 c_-=F_n^{-1}(1-\alpha-d),\qquad c_+=F_n^{-1}(1-\alpha+d).
\]
The Kolmogorov bound gives \(c_-\le\widehat c_n\le c_+\), while Gaussian concentration gives \(c_+\le\kappa_{m,n}+C_\alpha\).  The expansion and scale inequalities imply the deterministic inclusions
\[
 \{T_n\le(1-t)c_- -e\}
 \subseteq\{\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\}
 \subseteq\{T_n\le(1+t)c_+ +e\}.                                     \tag{26}
\]
For example, the left inclusion follows coordinatewise from
\[
 |\widehat\theta_{m,n,\ell}-\theta_{n,\ell}|/s_{m,n,\ell}
 \le T_n+e\le(1-t)c_-
 \le\widehat c_n\widehat s_{m,n,\ell}/s_{m,n,\ell};
\]
the reverse triangle inequality proves the other inclusion.

The anti-concentration part of \(\mathrm{lem{:}gaussian\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}comparison\mbox{-}anticoncentration}\), applied to the two threshold displacements in (26), now gives
\[
 \left|\Pr(\boldsymbol\theta_n\in\mathcal B_{m,n}\mid
 \mathcal F_n,\widehat d_{m,n})-(1-\alpha)\right|
 \le C_\alpha\{d+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)e+(\kappa_{m,n}+1)^2t\}.             \tag{27}
\]
This uses deterministic \(F_n\)-quantile brackets, so it remains valid although the score and fitted covariance use common data.  Uniform convergence in probability supplies deterministic \(e,t,d\downarrow0\) for which the complement of (25) is uniformly negligible and the right side of (27) vanishes.  Averaging the already-uniform conditional conclusion over the selected layout proves the conditional-on-\(\mathcal F_n\) assertion.  No covariance inverse is used.

For the advertised horizon, the Gaussian union bound and tail integration give \(\kappa_{m,n}\le C\sqrt{\log(2H_n)}\) for every correlation matrix.  At \(H_n=\lfloor n^{1/8}\rfloor\), the two preceding theorems give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{dir},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/2}\log n),
 &t_{\mathrm{dir},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}),\\
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{rec},n}&=O_{\Pr}(n^{-3/8}\log n+n^{-3/4}\log n),
 &t_{\mathrm{rec},n}\vee\Delta_{\mathrm{rec},n}
 &=O_{\Pr}(n^{-1/4}\sqrt{\log n}).
\end{aligned}                                                         \tag{28}
\]
The comparison part of the cited lemma yields
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rec},n}=O_{\Pr}\!\left(n^{-1/12}(\log n)^{5/6}\right)=o_{\Pr}(1),
\]
with a smaller direct error.  Multiplication by the displayed powers of \(\kappa_{m,n}+1\) shows that every term in the premise tends to zero.  Finally, simultaneous coverage implies pointwise coverage and, at \(H_n=1\), the construction equals the same Gaussian TWSF interval.  The strengthening concerns the whole conditional-mean path, not future realized prediction shocks.
